senses.def: An Italic tribe of northeast Latium and the central Apennines of Italy who appear in the early history of ancient Rome.
Of or relating to that ancient people who resided in Italy.
The Italic language spoken by the Aequi.
The case conveying an equality with another noun, equivalent to “like” or “as” in English. This case is used in some languages like Inuktitut.
Containing balanced proportions of saline, calcareous, ceraceous, aluminous, copper-bearing, and vitriolic constituents, especially descriptive of certain mineral waters.
ex: Aequeo­salino­calcalino­ceraceo­aluminoso­cupreo­vitriolic, at 52 letters, describing the spa waters at Bath, England, is attributed to Dr. Edward Strother (1675–1737).

senses.def: Having basidia maturing all over the surface of each lamella at once, not leaving patches of less matured spores.
Any pelagic hydrozoan of the genus Aequorea.
A photoprotein, isolated from luminescent jellyfish and other marine organisms, composed of two distinct units: the apoprotein apoaequorin and the prosthetic group coelenterazine.
